body: aider is AI pair programming in your terminal
plain_description: Aider turns your ideas into working code by pairing you with AI right in your terminal. It understands your entire codebase, makes surgical changes, and automatically commits them — so you ship faster without losing control. No need to leave your editor or learn a new workflow.
technical_description: Aider is an open-source AI pair programming tool that operates as a terminal-based CLI client written in Python. It connects to cloud LLMs (Claude, DeepSeek, OpenAI) or local models via API, performs repository-wide code analysis using a codebase map, and applies AI-suggested edits directly to source files. Features include automatic git commits with sensible messages, linting and test execution on changes, voice-to-code input, image and web page context ingestion, and IDE integration via file-watching. Installation is through pip with Docker available for containerized deployment.
title: Aider

body: CodeGeeX: An Open Multilingual Code Generation Model (KDD 2023)
plain_description: CodeGeeX boosts developer productivity by automatically generating, translating, and explaining code across 20+ programming languages. Deploy it as a VS Code or JetBrains extension for instant AI-powered code suggestions without leaving your editor. The open-source model runs on your own infrastructure or cloud GPUs, keeping your code data private.
technical_description: CodeGeeX is a 13-billion parameter autoregressive decoder-only transformer for multilingual code generation. The model contains 40 transformer layers with 5,120 hidden dimensions and 20,480 feed-forward dimensions, supporting 2,048-token sequences. It was pre-trained on 850 billion tokens across 23 programming languages on 1,536 Ascend 910 processors. CodeGeeX provides inference on NVIDIA GPUs (V100, A100) and Ascend 910, with quantization reducing GPU memory from 27 GB to 15 GB and INT8 acceleration achieving sub-15ms/token. It integrates with VS Code and JetBrains IDEs via extensions and supports containerized deployment through Docker.
title: CodeGeeX

plain_description: Continue is an AI coding agent that helps developers ship code faster without leaving their existing tools — VS Code, JetBrains, or terminal. It is open source, so there is no vendor lock-in or per-seat licensing fees. The bottom line: your team gets AI-assisted development that integrates where you already work.
technical_description: Continue is an open-source AI coding agent implemented in TypeScript. It runs as a VS Code extension, JetBrains plugin, and standalone CLI, connecting to local or remote language models through a configurable provider interface. The core engine manages context retrieval, code indexing, autocomplete generation, inline editing, and multi-step agent workflows, communicating with IDE hosts via a message protocol. It supports MCP (Model Context Protocol) for extensible tool integration and includes a React-based GUI rendered inside the IDE.
title: Continue

body: DeepSeek Coder: Let the Code Write Itself
plain_description: DeepSeek Coder is a family of AI models that write, complete, and debug code across nearly 100 programming languages. It helps developers ship faster with state-of-the-art code generation, project-level autocomplete, and a chat interface for programming questions.
technical_description: DeepSeek Coder is a series of code language models (1B to 33B parameters) pre-trained from scratch on 2T tokens (87% code, 13% natural language in English and Chinese). Models use a 16K-token window and a fill-in-the-blank training objective for project-level code completion and infilling. Inference runs via the HuggingFace Transformers library with PyTorch and CUDA, or via vLLM for high-throughput serving. The repository provides scripts for fine-tuning with DeepSpeed and supports GGUF quantization via llama.cpp and GPTQ via exllamav2. A demo is available on Hugging Face Spaces and can be run locally.
title: DeepSeek-Coder

plain_description: Generate high-quality code across 600+ programming languages with a model trained on 4+ trillion tokens. It handles code completion, infilling, and generation tasks out of the box. The bottom line: get production-ready code suggestions without building your own model.
technical_description: StarCoder2-15B is a 15-billion-parameter causal language model trained on The Stack v2 dataset using the Fill-in-the-Middle objective. It implements a transformer decoder architecture with grouped-query attention and a 16,384-token context window with 4,096-token sliding window attention. The model is distributed via Hugging Face Transformers, supports CPU and GPU inference, and offers quantized inference through bitsandbytes (8-bit and 4-bit). It was trained with the NVIDIA NeMo Framework on 1024 H100 GPUs.
title: StarCoder2

plain_description: Tabby is a self-hosted AI coding assistant that helps your developers write code faster while keeping all data on your own infrastructure. No per-seat fees and no external cloud dependency. Your team gets AI-powered code completion and chat backed by your private codebase.
technical_description: Tabby is a self-hosted AI coding assistant server written in Rust. It provides code completion and conversational chat via an OpenAPI-compatible REST interface. The server runs as a single self-contained binary or Docker container with no external database or cloud service dependencies. Inference supports consumer-grade NVIDIA GPUs via CUDA and Apple Silicon via Metal, with CPU fallback. Tabby integrates with IDEs including VSCode, IntelliJ, Vim, and Eclipse through LSP-based plugins and exposes an OpenAPI specification for custom integrations. Key capabilities include RAG-based code completion using repository context, an Answer Engine for engineering knowledge retrieval, and a web-based administration UI for team management, SSO, and configuration.
title: Tabby
